back_translation: Open your doors, O Lebanon, that fire may consume your cedars!
Wail, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen; the majestic trees are ruined! Wail, O oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest has been cut down!
Listen to the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is in ruins! Listen to the roaring of the young lions, for the thicket of the Jordan is destroyed!
This is what the LORD my God says: “Shepherd the flock marked for slaughter.
Those who buy them slaughter them without remorse, and those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be the LORD, for I am rich!’ And their own shepherds have no pity on them.

For I will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land,” declares the LORD. “Behold, I will hand over every man into the hand of his neighbor and his king; they will crush the land, and I will not deliver it from their hand.”
So I shepherded the flock marked for slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. And I took two staffs: one I called Favor, the other I called Union; and I shepherded the flock.
In one month I cut off the three shepherds. My soul grew impatient with the flock, and their soul also detested me.
So I said, “I will not shepherd you. Let the dying die, and the perishing perish; and let those that remain devour one another’s flesh.”
Then I took my staff called Favor and cut it in two, breaking the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
It was broken on that day, and so the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that it was the word of the LORD.
Then I said to them, “If it seems right to you, give me my wages; but if not, keep them.” So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.
And the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter”—the magnificent price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter in the house of the LORD.
Then I cut in two my second staff called Union, breaking the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
And the LORD said to me, “Take up once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

For behold, I am raising up a shepherd in the land who will not care for the perishing, nor seek the young, nor heal the broken, nor sustain the healthy, but will eat the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hooves.
Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock! May a sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm be utterly withered and his right eye completely blinded!
